transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm mostly here because the clinic got on me about how little I've been eating lately. But honestly, most days I'm just grabbing a coffee before my shift at the warehouse, and then maybe a yogurt or just a few bites of something after my GED class. It's just... sitting down for an actual, full meal feels like it throws off everything I'm trying to keep in line right now.
Have you lost any weight recently?

Yeah, I have. My work pants are pretty loose right now, and people keep telling me I look too thin. But honestly... when I step on the scale and see the number go down, I just feel like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don't really see why I should be pushed to put the weight back on when I'm actually making progress.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah, I am. I mean... if I eat something heavy, like the fried food they sometimes leave in the break room at work, or a big plate of food at church, I get really scared that it’s going to show on me right away. I'll just keep thinking about it the rest of the day, and it bothers me until I can go check the scale to make sure.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within an hour?

No, I don't really do that. Like I said, I mostly just stick to my coffee and maybe a yogurt. Eating a big amount of food like that all at once... that's not something I do. I'd be way too worried about it.
Do you think your weight is currently at a healthy level?

I think it's fine. I know my regular doctor and some people from church are worried, but... honestly, I think they’re making a bigger deal out of it than it really is. I mean, I’m still going to work, I'm doing my classes, and I'm keeping up with my life just fine. If my weight was really a problem, I wouldn't be able to do all of that.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?
No, not really. Since I don't really eat big meals anyway, I don't ever feel like I'm losing control. I always know exactly what I'm eating.
Do you think you would be a failure if you gained weight?

Yeah, I think I would. I mean, when I look in the mirror before class or before I go play softball, my stomach and my thighs still look bigger than they should be. How I look right then kind of decides everything. It can make me feel like I’m either doing good or just... failing for the whole day. So if I actually gained weight, yeah, I would definitely feel like a failure.
Do you think that even if you were at a healthy weight, you would still want to lose more weight?

Yeah, I probably would. I'm just... I'm really scared of gaining anything. Like, if I eat something like fried food from the break room at work, or a big plate of food at church, I get scared it’s going to show on me right away. I'll just keep thinking about it and I'll want to check the scale. So, yeah, I think I'd always want to lose a little more just to make sure that doesn't happen.
Do you think that if you were at a weight that most people would consider healthy, you would still see yourself as overweight when you look in the mirror?

I'm not really sure. I mean, it's hard to say since I haven't been at a weight like that in a long time. I don't really know what I would see in the mirror if I was at... whatever people call a healthy weight. I just know what I see right now.
Do you think you would still see yourself as overweight even if other people told you that you look healthy?

Yeah, I think I would. It kind of goes back to what I was saying a minute ago. When I look in the mirror, like before class or before I play softball, my stomach and my thighs just still look bigger than they should to me. It wouldn't really matter what someone else told me, because what I see right then is what makes me feel like I'm either doing good or just failing for the whole day. So, yeah, I'd still see myself as bigger no matter what other people say.
Do you think your perception of your own body shape and weight is different from how others see you?

Yeah, I do. I mean, it goes right back to what I was just saying a second ago. When I look in the mirror, like before class or softball, my stomach and my thighs still look bigger than they should to me. Other people might not see that, but I do. And what I see in the mirror right then... it just makes me feel like I’m either doing good or completely failing for the whole day. So, yeah, I guess how I see myself is probably pretty different from how they see me.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours, without being able to stop once you started?
No, I don't really do that. I don't think I've ever eaten a huge amount of food all at once like that, or felt like I couldn't stop. I usually just try to keep things pretty controlled.
Do you think your weight or body shape is the most important aspect of your self-worth?

Yeah, I really do. Like I keep bringing up... when I check the mirror before class or softball and see my stomach and thighs looking too big, it just dictates everything for me. It literally makes me feel like I'm either doing good or just completely failing at life for the whole day. So, yeah, my weight and how my body looks is pretty much the main thing I base my worth on.
Is your goal to be as thin as possible?

Yeah, pretty much. I mean, my work pants are loose right now, and people keep saying I look too thin... but honestly, when I see the number on the scale go down, I just feel like I’m finally getting somewhere. It feels like progress. So I really don’t see why I should be pushed to put the weight back on.
Have you experienced any changes in your menstrual cycle?
No, I haven't really noticed any changes with that. My period has just been pretty normal, honestly.
Is there a specific part of your body that you are most concerned about when you think about gaining weight?

Not really one specific part, no. I mean, I know I mentioned my stomach and thighs earlier, but honestly... I just don't want to gain weight anywhere. It's the whole thing. I just don't want to get bigger overall, so it's not like I'm only worried about one spot.
Do you think gaining weight would affect your relationships or how people perceive you?

I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it like that. I mean, people already tell me I look too thin, so I guess if I gained weight they might just stop bothering me about it. But honestly, it's not really about them or how they see me. It's just about how I feel about myself. So no, I don't think it would really change my relationships.
Have you ever felt like you've eaten an amount of food that's much larger than most people would eat in a short period of time?

No, I haven't. I mean... I don't really eat much to begin with, so I've never had a time where I ate a huge amount of food like that. It's pretty much always the exact opposite for me. I just stick to small amounts.
